#2171. Chelsea co-sporting director Laurence Stewart to leave in leadership reshuffle

Gary Gowers is a sports journalist and the editor of Read Everton, where he leads daily coverage of Everton news, transfers and analysis. He also writes about Manchester City for Read Man City and motorsport for Read Motorsport. A former accountant, he became a freelance writer in 2011 and has written for BBC Sport and Metro.

Laurence Stewart is set to leave Chelsea by mutual consent after almost four years at Stamford Bridge, with the club opting to redistribute his responsibilities rather than appoint a direct replacement.

The departure is understood to be amicable and won’t take immediate effect. Stewart could continue attending matches before formally leaving, following discussions with co-owner Behdad Eghbali over the club’s evolving sporting structure.

The story was first reported by Matt Law of The Telegraph and Nizaar Kinsella of BBC Sport, with Ben Jacobs subsequently providing further details about how Chelsea intend to operate.

Stewart arrived from Monaco in October 2022 as technical director before becoming co-sporting director alongside Paul Winstanley in February 2023.

Chelsea’s day-to-day sporting leadership will now be shared between Winstanley, Sam Jewell and Joe Shields, each with defined responsibilities.

Winstanley will continue overseeing transfer negotiations, player contracts and several departments at Cobham, including medical and performance operations. Shields’ work centres on the academy and player pathways, while Jewell has wider responsibilities across the BlueCo operation, including Strasbourg.

According to Jacobs, discussions about restructuring began in April and accelerated following the appointment of Xabi Alonso as head coach.

Stewart had overseen investment in Chelsea’s data analysis operation, although Jewell and Shields have increasingly taken responsibility for using that information in recruitment and talent identification.

Dave Fallows will remain involved in an advisory capacity, rather than taking on a fixed day-to-day portfolio.

The changes are being described as a natural evolution of Chelsea’s sporting model. There is no suggestion that Stewart’s departure followed a breakdown in relations, and the club are not currently planning to recruit a replacement.

#2170. Queens Park Rangers vs Lincoln City - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ben Sully | 05 Nov 2026 17:09, Last updated: 05 Nov 2026 17:10

Queens Park Rangers will face Lincoln City for the first time in 55 years when the two sides lock horns at Loftus Road on Saturday.

The R's are currently sitting in 11th place in the Championship table, while the visitors start the weekend in 19th position.

QPR may be one point adrift of the top eight, but they have found wins hard to come by over the last couple of months, having won just two of their last 10 matches.

The most recent of those victories came via an emphatic 5-0 scoreline against Swansea City, only to fall to a heavy 4-1 loss away to Southampton a week later.

Julien Stephan's side took a point from their latest outing against Burnley, with Jonathan Varane netting a second-half equaliser in a 1-1 draw at Loftus Road on Tuesday.

They should fancy their chances of picking up at least another point from Saturday's fixture, considering they have lost just one of their seven home league games this season (W3, D3).

A sturdy backline has helped provide the foundation for their strong home form, having conceded just six goals in their seven outings at Loftus Road, with only two teams letting in fewer on home turf.

While they have not faced Lincoln since 1971, QPR have won four of their previous six official meetings with the Imps (D1, L1).

Lincoln, meanwhile, are focusing on preserving their Championship status in their first season in the second tier since the 1960-61 season.

The Imps are currently sitting five points above the bottom three after winning four, drawing three and losing seven of their 14 Championship outings this season.

They have struggled to add to their points tally in recent times, having lost five of their previous seven matches, including their last two outings against Birmingham and Watford.

The Imps fell to a 3-1 home loss against Blues last weekend, before they were beaten by a narrow 1-0 scoreline in their midweek away clash against the Hornets.

As a result of Tuesday's loss, Chris Cohen and Tom Shaw's side have now gone three away games without a win since starting the Championship campaign with three consecutive victories on the road.

They have the league's joint third-best defensive away record with eight goals conceded, although they have netted just six times on their travels in the Championship this term.

QPR forward Alfie Jones will be out until the new year after sustaining a hamstring injury in the defeat to Southampton last weekend.

The R’s are also without the services of Amadou Mbengue, Tariq Lamptey, Nicolas Madsen and Rumarn Burrell, while there are doubts surrounding Jake Clarke-Salter’s availability.

Richard Kone, who has netted four goals in the last three games, is expected to be available for selection despite appearing to be forced off with a physical issue in the midweek draw with Burnley.

As for the Imps, they remain without the injured duo of Tendayi Darikwa and Mason Melia, while Conor McGrandles is a doubt after missing the last two matches.

Forward Ben House will drop out of the squad to serve a one-match ban after picking up his fifth yellow card of the Championship season in Tuesday’s defeat to Watford.

Lincoln are hopeful that Mikkel Ladefoged and Ethan Wheatley will prove their fitness in time for the trip to Loftus Road.

Queens Park Rangers possible starting lineup:

Charles; Adamson, Dunne, Edwards, Kemper; Poku, Varane, Kamara, Vale; Kone, Smyth

Wickens; Coubis, Elerewe, Bradley, Reach; Konak, Varfolomeev; Hackett, Street, Jefferies; Draper

QPR may not be in the best of form, but they have proven to be a tough team to beat on home turf this term, and considering Lincoln have lost five of their last seven matches, we think the signs points to a home win on Saturday.

Arsenal have received a significant boost with William Saliba returning to first-team training. He’s spent almost four months out with a back injury.

The French international was seen returning to training on the pitch. Sparking hope that he could be back in action soon for Mikel Arteta.

Saliba has been sidelined since he suffered the injury in France’s 2-0 semi-final defeat to Spain. The defender was forced off after only 30 minutes after playing the full 90 in his previous five starts at the tournament.

The player was confirmed by Arsenal to be sidelined for a lengthy period of time in July. He did not require surgery, meaning he can begin working back into action.

His latest progress comes at an important point in Arsenal’s season, with several major fixtures approaching.

The 25-year-old has travelled to the Czech Republic with Arsenal’s squad to face Slavia Prague in the Champions League.

Arteta confirmed that Saliba had played for 45 minutes in a behind-closed-moors game last week as part of his rehab.

He then returned to full first team training on Tuesday, providing another defensive option for the club.

The Arsenal manager has not confirmed if the Frenchman will be involved tonight.

His return to training is a major step in his road to full fitness, but it remains to be seen if he will play against Slavia Prague tonight.

#2167. Slavia Prague 1-2 Arsenal: Madueke and Gyokeres fire Gunners to Champions League victory

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal moved up to third in the Champions League table after beating Slavia Prague 2-1 at the Fortuna Arena.

Noni Madueke opened the scoring after nine minutes, finishing calmly after Viktor Gyokeres sent him through on goal.

The Swedish striker then doubled Arsenal’s advantage with an excellent finish in the 38th minute. However, a much stronger second-half performance from Slavia made for an uncomfortable finish.

Wiktor Nowak scored a late goal to put pressure on the Gunners. They held on to take all three points.

Mikel Arteta made six changes from the Liverpool win on Sunday. William Saliba returns to the squad after his back injury.

The defender was left on the bench, with Ezri Konsa playing alongside Gabriel Magalhães in central defence.

Arsenal started brightly and took control of the game when they won the long ball forward. Gyokeres beat his man and found Madueke with a clever through ball.

The winger used his pace to get into the penalty area before sliding his finish through goalkeeper Nazar Domchak’s legs.

Arsenal continued to create chances, with Mikel Merino going close on several occasions. Domchak also produced an important save to deny the midfielder from close range.

Merino eventually helped Arsenal extend their lead. After winning possession in the Slavia half, Declan Rice found Gyokeres, who exchanged passes with the Spaniard before curling a superb finish into the far corner.

The visitors could have added a third before the break. Gabriel’s header from a corner was cleared off the line.

Arsenal appeared to be in control at half-time.

But Slavia upped the tempo and started to create more space, forcing Arsenal into a defensive stance. Early on, Oskar Kubiak fired a long-range shot, forcing David Raya to push it away.

Arteta got increasingly frustrated as Arsenal struggled to hold on to the ball and dominate the midfield.

They tried to keep pressing, but Arsenal struggled to create much at the other end. Madueke did get into a good position to shoot from an angle but didn’t have enough power to cause any problems for Domchak.

Slavia were denied a goal when Gabriel headed the ball away from the goal line. Raya made a brilliant stop to keep the shot out while the penalty area was crowded.

The Arsenal keeper made another stunning save as Kubiak powered a header from a cross. Raya deflected the ball onto the post to keep his team ahead by two goals.

Slavia scored their breakthrough goal in the 90th minute after David Jurasek played a low cross from the left. Nowak was able to run into the box to score past Raya.

It created a nervy few minutes of added time as Arsenal had to defend their lead.

Slavia could find no way back into the game as Stepan Chaloupek headed wide and Mikulas Konecny threatened in the dying moments, but his effort lacked confidence as Raya made light work of saving.

Arsenal secured their third win in their last four Champions League games to move to 10 points and into third place in the group stage.

The Gunners have now gone unbeaten in their last ten Champions League away games to set a new club record.

However, Arteta will be looking for a much better display from his side when they resume action in the Premier League against Hull City on Saturday.

#2166. The Good, The Bad and The Ugly of Scott Parker’s Managerial Career

With Scott Parker now in the manager’s seat, supporters are naturally asking the same question: what exactly will a Parker team look like?

Last night gave us a glimpse of his ability to deliver a rousing half-time team talk, but what else can he bring to the table besides a penchant for pricey cardigans?

His managerial career has established a clear tactical identity, one that has delivered success in the Championship but has also attracted criticism at higher levels.

Gonzo has already covered this in a previous article, citing that Parker typically favours either a 4-2-3-1 or 4-3-3 formation, built around organisation, possession and defensive discipline.

His teams are usually constructed from the back, with an emphasis on retaining control of the ball rather than engaging in frenetic, end-to-end football. The objective is often to dominate territory through patient build-up play, moving possession into wide areas to stretch opponents before creating openings.

Defensively, Parker’s sides tend to be compact and difficult to break down. A double pivot in midfield frequently provides protection for the back line, allowing his teams to maintain their shape and reduce space between the lines.

The philosophy is clear: control games first, take risks second.

While that approach has often proved effective in the Championship, critics argue it can sometimes become overly cautious, particularly when chasing games or facing stronger opposition.

One aspect of Parker’s CV cannot be ignored: he knows how to get out of the Championship.

He guided Fulham to promotion through the play-offs in 2020 and followed that by leading Bournemouth to automatic promotion in 2022. His ability to organise teams over the course of a demanding Championship season is well established.

For a West Ham side whose only objective is a return to the Premier League, that experience was undoubtedly a major factor behind the club’s decision.

The bigger question is whether he can combine results with the attacking football supporters crave.

Will Parker get West Ham on the front foot?

At Fulham, supporters generally look back on Parker’s spell with a degree of respect.

Promotion to the Premier League remains a significant achievement, but frustration grew during the following campaign as the football became increasingly conservative. Despite periods of decent organisation, Fulham were ultimately relegated and some supporters felt the team’s cautious approach limited its potential.

With regards to his time at Bournemouth, Parker’s stock was initially high on the south coast after guiding the club back to the Premier League at the first attempt.

However, his relationship with supporters deteriorated rapidly following promotion. Public criticism of the club’s transfer business and squad depth, particularly after a heavy 9-0 defeat at Liverpool, created tensions that cost him his job.

His dismissal divided opinion, especially after Gary O’Neil kept Bournemouth comfortably in the Premier League with largely the same group of players.

Parker’s short tenure in Belgium at Club Brugge proved to be the most difficult period of his managerial career.

Expectations were high upon his arrival, but results and performances failed to follow. His tactical approach was widely criticised and he struggled to adapt quickly enough to the demands of Belgian football.

The experiment was brought to an abrupt end after only a brief spell in charge.

Burnley supporters largely viewed Parker’s appointment through a practical lens.

His track record of Championship promotions offered reassurance, but concerns remained over whether his style could provide the excitement and attacking intent fans wanted to see.

As with many clubs that have employed Parker, appreciation for results was often balanced against questions surrounding entertainment value.

That said, I actually know a Burnley fan, and when Parker was appointed, he messaged me just two words: “Good appointment!”

The challenge facing Parker at West Ham is clear. We arguably possess one of the strongest squads in the division and supporters will expect more than simply grinding out results. Promotion remains the priority, but fans will also want to see an identity return to the team after the uncertainty of the Nuno Espírito Santo era.

One thing is certain: after months of instability, West Ham have turned to a manager with a proven track record at this level.

Now comes the difficult part. Turning potential into winning games!

Now he’s in, let’s unite behind him and see where he can take us. COYI!

I have been a season ticket holder since the late eighties, so experienced the highs and lows of being a West Ham supporter. I previously wrote for OLAS and have contributed to a number of football publications in the past.

Our current goalkeeper has not laid a hand on the last nine goals he has let in. Virtually every corner if he makes a parry out, it is always at 90 degree angle to our goal, so making an assist for the opposition, who have gone on to score from this assist. Ex professional goalkeeper Nuno, could not help this boy change his bad habits, surely Scott has already realised changes start with the goalkeeper

Scott’s style of play will have to be adapted to utilise to the full the talents of this current squad.

This will be a totally bespoke solution to the formation conundrum. Scott is up to the task in hand. When he had gained promotion with the other three teams, they sold his best players and expected him to work miracles whilst remaining silent about the circumstances.

Considering the rug-pulling, Scott did a great job at each club. With some support to enhance and progress the playing staff available to him he would have been well established as a leading PL manager by now.

I still believe he has the attributes to be that leading PL manager and I hope that will be whilst in the employ of West Ham.

By Carter White | 05 Nov 2026 17:09

Aiming to record three consecutive successes at their Highbury Stadium fortress, Fleetwood Town host fellow League Two outfit Rochdale for a clash in the first round of the FA Cup on Saturday afternoon.

The Cod Army have taken Arsenal's scalp on home soil in recent times in the EFL Cup, whilst the Dale are struggling to get a grip on the fourth tier following their promotion from the National League.

Despite mulling around in the lower reaches of the League Two standings since their League One relegation in 2024, Fleetwood Town have enjoyed the spotlight recently after a historic cup success.

On October 27, the Cod Army welcomed Premier League champions Arsenal to Highbury and knocked their visitors out of the EFL Cup, with the hosts earning a quarter-final tie with Everton in the middle of December.

Scoring in both the beating of the Gunners and last weekend's 3-1 third-tier victory over Bristol Rovers, Aaron Loupalo-Bi is experiencing a breakthrough campaign in senior football, with the Fulham loanee netting five competitive goals for Fleetwood so far.

That success over the Gasmen last time out extended the Cod Army's unbeaten run at Highbury Stadium to five matches (W4 D1) in all competitions, whilst Matt Lawlor's men have lost just once across seven home league contests to date.

Rather unsurprisingly, that sole Lancashire loss came at the hands of Saturday's visitors Rochdale in September, when first-half efforts from Dajaune Brown and Aden Flint sealed maximum League Two points for the Dale.

Rochdale are back in the EFL this campaign following a three-year absence, winning the National League playoff final over Boreham Wood at Wembley Stadium, with that particular clash decided by penalty kicks.

Since returning, the Dale have failed to distance themselves from an impending relegation dogfight, with Saturday afternoon's visitors in the midst of a seven-game winless run (D2 L5) across League Two and EFL Trophy duties.

Alarmingly, Ian Watson's men have lost each of their past three competitive contests by an aggregate scoreline of 13-3, suffering a 4-1 EFL Trophy defeat by Doncaster Rovers at Crown Oil Arena on Tuesday night.

Last tasting fourth-tier success on October 3 at home to Swindon Town, Rochdale have slumped down to 20th spot in the League Two table, just three points above 23rd-placed Colchester United.

Runners-up in the EFL Cup in 1962, the Dale have not enjoyed such success in the FA Cup and last season's attempt at glory ended in the fourth qualifying round at the hands of York City.

Scoring Fleetwood's third goal in the win over Bristol Rovers, midfielder Josh Robertson is pushing for a rare start this weekend.

The Cod Army could involve attacker Will Davies from the start on Saturday, with the 27-year-old providing an assist against the Gasmen last time out.

A hero at wing-back for Fleetwood in their conquering of Arsenal in the EFL Cup, Scotsman Shaun Rooney should start in a more natural centre-back role on Saturday.

Captaining Rochdale at the age of 41 earlier in the week, Ian Henderson should keep his spot at the focal point of attack.

That being said, the Dale will be keen to get Derby County loanee Brown back into the starting XI for a winner-takes-all clash at Highbury.

Lynch; Rooney, Bennett, Potter; McLean, Neal, Helm, McCann, Batty; Coughlan, Loupalo-Bi

Waller; Sherring, Flint, Wilson, Tasker; Adeeko, Gilmour; Hannot, Francis; Henderson, Brown

Following their historic home success over Arsenal last month, Fleetwood will be extremely confident of repeating the trick against a fellow League Two side this weekend.

Rochdale have conceded 18 goals across their past five matches and are unlikely to keep the Cod Army at bay on Saturday.

#2163. Arsenal injury latest: Konsa concern, Saliba return and Saka update

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal will hope Ezri Konsa recovers in time for Saturday’s 3pm Premier League clash with Hull City after he came off during their Champions League win over Slavia Prague.The return of William Saliba to the matchday squad is a great boost for Mikel Arteta ahead of the game, but Bukayo Saka remains out as he continues to recover from his quad injury.

Here is all the latest Arsenal injury news and when the three players are expected to return.

Konsa started Arsenal’s 2-1 victory over Slavia Prague on Wednesday but came off in the second half after experiencing discomfort.

He appeared to limp during the first half, so Arsenal will monitor his fitness closely ahead of Saturday’s match.

Arteta said the change was not a tactical one, as Konsa had been playing a lot of games recently and had some problems during the match.

The Arsenal boss is likely to give an update ahead of Saturday’s game depending on how he recovers in the coming days.

Konsa’s absence will leave Arsenal without as many reliable centre backs. However, Gabriel will play a key role in the backline, and Arteta has other options in Cristhian Mosquera and Piero Hincapie.

Potential return date: November 7 vs Hull City (3pm kick-off).

A positive from the Gunners’ trip to Prague was the inclusion of Saliba in the squad.

The defender has not played this season after picking up a long-term back injury. The issue got worse during his time with France at the World Cup finals, but he managed to avoid surgery.

Saliba has steadily built up his workload and played for 45 minutes in a behind-closed-moors game. He returned to full training on Tuesday and travelled with the squad to take on Slavia Prague.

Although he did not come off the bench, his inclusion shows he is getting close to being back in contention.

Arteta said that Saliba was feeling confident, but it will depend on the needs of the squad.

It gives Arsenal an extra experienced centre-back, and if Konsa is not available against Hull, then he could make an appearance on the pitch.

Potential return date: November 7 vs Hull City (3pm kick-off).

Saka is currently the main attacking concern for Arsenal after he has been sidelined with a quad injury for the last four games.

The winger suffered the injury approximately 10 minutes into the Arsenal Champions League clash against Bayern Munich last month.

The original fears were that Saka would be out for up to eight weeks. Arsenal have not given any confirmation on how long it will take him to make a full recovery.

He will need to undergo another scan to get a better idea of the amount of swelling and fluid in the area. The medical staff will also want to see if the tendon is involved.

This means it is unlikely he plays against Hull. Arsenal are not expected to bring him back too quickly ahead of the international break.

Arteta will miss one of his most influential attackers. Hopefully the next scan will give a clearer indication of how long he is likely to be out for.

Expected return date: Unknown. Saka is not expected to face Hull City on November 7.

Arsenal host Hull City at the Emirates Stadium on Saturday, November 7th.

The game comes ahead of a tough sequence of games which sees Manchester City, Real Madrid and Tottenham on the horizon. Arteta will want as many defensive and attacking threats on hand.

#2162. Chelsea make early move for Palmeiras teenager Eduardo Conceicao

Gary Gowers is a sports journalist and the editor of Read Everton, where he leads daily coverage of Everton news, transfers and analysis. He also writes about Manchester City for Read Man City and motorsport for Read Motorsport. A former accountant, he became a freelance writer in 2011 and has written for BBC Sport and Metro.

Chelsea have reportedly made contact with Palmeiras as they attempt to gain an early advantage in the race to sign Brazilian teenager Eduardo Conceicao.

The 16-year-old forward has attracted attention from several leading European clubs, but Chelsea are understood to be among the first to establish direct contact with Palmeiras over a potential future transfer.

According to Mark Brus of CaughtOffside, the London club have held a series of discussions as they seek to position themselves ahead of their rivals.

Palmeiras are reportedly preparing for substantial offers, with some figures at the Brazilian club discussing a valuation as high as €100m (£85m).

That figure has not been established as a firm asking price, however, and Brus reports that industry sources expect the eventual cost to be lower. Chelsea’s previous investment of approximately £51m in Estevao is regarded as a possible benchmark.

Manchester City’s ownership group have also made contact regarding Conceicao, while Arsenal, Manchester United, Barcelona, Real Madrid, Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain are among the clubs reported to have watched him.

Chelsea’s existing relationship with Palmeiras could help their efforts, although the level of competition means there is no guarantee that their early interest will lead to a deal.

The player’s age is another consideration. Conceicao cannot complete an international transfer to England until he turns 18, leaving interested clubs facing a potentially lengthy wait before he can join their squads.

Chelsea have already demonstrated their willingness to agree deals for young players well before they are eligible to arrive, with Estevao providing a particularly relevant example.

No formal bid or agreement has been reported for Conceicao. Nevertheless, the latest claims suggest Chelsea are prepared to explore another long-term investment in Brazilian talent rather than wait until the player becomes available for an immediate move.

#2160. Returning star makes 'up my game' admission amid striker battle

Joe Westley believes his battle for game time with fellow Dundee attackers will only benefit the Tayside club.

With just one defeat in the last five, the Dark Blues are in fifth place in the William Hill Premiership and the fourth-highest scorers, with Ashley Hay notching three in the last four games and Bradley Fink with four in the last six.

Westley missed three games with an ankle injury but replaced Fink in the 3-1 win over Kilmarnock last Wednesday and, ahead of the Tayside derby against St Johnstone at McDiarmid Park on Saturday, the 22-year-old, with five goals in all competitions this season, said: “I think it’s a healthy competition.

“Everyone wants to be playing football and be in the team. So when we’ve got Ash and Brad scoring, it means I need to up my game and score as many as I can when I’m given the chance because you know that when you’ve got the shirt, people are waiting to take it off you.

“It’s a healthy competition and I think we all drive each other to be the best versions of ourselves.

“I think when all the strikers are scoring and doing well, it’s good to be a part of an attack that’s doing well because you create for each other. If everyone’s firing and everyone’s doing well, then it increases your chance of getting goals and assisting as well.

“It’s a really good time to be an attacker at the club. I think it’s starting to click between everyone and whoever’s on up front has got a great understanding of what’s wanted from them. It gives them the best possible chance to score goals and win games.

“I think everything can come down to hard work. As a group everyone around the club works so hard day in, day out and we’re pushed in training, we’re pushed in the gym and I think we try and always gain the little one percent that we can every week.

“But also there’s the environment that the manager has created where everyone’s in it together. Everyone wants to do the hard yards for each other and I think the hard yards and the basics of football are things that can separate you from other teams in the league.

“I think so far this season we’ve been good at the basics and as long as we continue to do them we’ll be fine.”

#2159. Chelsea news: Stewart departure, Scott interest and Bournemouth preparations

Gary Gowers is a sports journalist and the editor of Read Everton, where he leads daily coverage of Everton news, transfers and analysis. He also writes about Manchester City for Read Man City and motorsport for Read Motorsport. A former accountant, he became a freelance writer in 2011 and has written for BBC Sport and Metro.

Chelsea’s sporting department is facing another change following news of Laurence Stewart’s impending departure, while the club continue to be linked with potential additions to their squad.

Alex Scott and Palmeiras teenager Eduardo Conceicao have both featured in Thursday’s transfer coverage, with Xabi Alonso also preparing his players for Saturday’s Premier League meeting with Bournemouth.

Here is our 7pm round-up of the latest Chelsea news for Thursday, 8 October.

Laurence Stewart is set to leave Chelsea by mutual consent after almost four years at Stamford Bridge, with the club planning to redistribute his responsibilities rather than appoint a direct replacement.

His departure is understood to be amicable and will not take immediate effect. Stewart joined from Monaco in 2022, initially as technical director, before becoming co-sporting director alongside Paul Winstanley.

As detailed in our report on Stewart’s departure and Chelsea’s leadership reshuffle, Winstanley, Sam Jewell and Joe Shields are expected to take on expanded responsibilities across recruitment, player development and the wider BlueCo operation.

The changes follow discussions about the club’s sporting structure that reportedly began earlier this year. There is no confirmed suggestion that Stewart’s departure resulted from a disagreement with Alonso.

Chelsea’s reported interest in Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott remains a talking point, despite the south coast club’s determination to retain the England international.

The Blues reportedly had a £64m offer rejected during the summer, with Matt Law of The Telegraph subsequently identifying Chelsea as leading contenders for the 23-year-old.

However, as examined in our latest report on Chelsea’s interest in Scott, Bournemouth are not expected to entertain a January sale.

Scott’s immediate concern is recovering from a thigh injury suffered while representing England. The midfielder could face several weeks on the sidelines, potentially complicating Bournemouth’s plans as well as any future discussions about his next move.

Chelsea have also reportedly made contact with Palmeiras over 16-year-old forward Eduardo Conceicao, who is attracting attention from several leading European clubs.

According to Mark Brus of CaughtOffside, Chelsea have held discussions with the Brazilian club as they explore the possibility of a future deal.

Our report on Chelsea’s interest in Eduardo Conceicao explains that a valuation as high as €100m has been suggested, although that figure is not a confirmed asking price or evidence of a formal bid.

Manchester City, Arsenal and Real Madrid are among the other clubs reportedly monitoring the teenager. Conceicao would be unable to complete a transfer to England until he turns 18, making any prospective move a longer-term consideration.

Alonso’s attention will now turn to Saturday’s Premier League meeting with Bournemouth at Stamford Bridge.

The match kicks off at 3pm and will not be televised live in the United Kingdom because of the Saturday afternoon broadcasting blackout.

Our Chelsea v Bournemouth kick-off and how-to-watch guide provides the full details, including how to follow the match and the available overseas broadcast information.

Scott’s injury is expected to deprive Bournemouth of an important midfield option, although Chelsea will have their own fitness decisions to make as players return from international duty.

After Saturday’s fixture, Chelsea travel to Hill Dickinson Stadium to face Everton on 17 October. Alonso will be looking for greater consistency as the domestic programme resumes.

#2158. West Bromwich Albion vs Millwall - prediction, team news, lineups

By Carter White | 05 Nov 2026 17:44, Last updated: 07 Nov 2026 11:12

Aiming to record their maiden home success of November, West Bromwich Albion welcome struggling Millwall to The Hawthorns for an all-important Championship clash on Saturday afternoon.

The Baggies shared the spoils with promotion rivals Southampton earlier in the week in the Black Country, whilst the Lions were tamed by Max Bird and Birmingham City further East in the West Midlands.

Since a disappointing derby defeat by Birmingham on October 10, West Brom have strung together an impressive five-game unbeaten run (W3 D2) in the Championship, suggesting that the Baggies are genuine promotion contenders this campaign.

One of the pre-season title favourites were forced to split the points at The Hawthorns on Tuesday night, when Samuel Edozie's first Southampton goal since the 2023-24 term was not enough to defeat the hosts.

Scoring the opener from the penalty spot against the Saints earlier in the week, Isaac Price has joined summer arrival Jimmy-Jay Morgan on five second-tier goals at the beginning of this campaign.

Despite a lack of quality wide attackers, James Morrison's side are competent in forward areas, scoring thrice in a statement victory at the base of West Ham United last Saturday afternoon.

Tipped by pundits and supporters alike for a campaign of midtable mediocrity, the Baggies are currently occupying sixth spot in the Championship rankings, just two points behind arch rivals Wolverhampton Wanderers in second.

After being within a whisker of earning automatic promotion to the Premier League in May, Millwall have endured a fall from grace at the start of this campaign, with this weekend's visitors winning just two of their past eight matches (D3 L3).

The Lions were unable to build on their Halloween battering of Derby at St Andrew's @ Knighthead Park on Tuesday night, when first-half goals from Alex Cochrane, Bird and Jay Stansfield sealed a comfortable victory for in-form Birmingham.

Defeated in four of their opening seven league outings (W2 D1) in 2026-27, Alex Neil's side have now lost as many away matches as they did across the entire span of last season, when Millwall were the division's best travellers.

Only beating the league's basement boys in Preston North End and Derby since the middle of September, the Lions have slumped down to 13th spot in the Championship table, five points behind eighth-placed West Ham.

Despite the understandable doom and gloom at the moment, Millwall have cause for optimism ahead of Saturday's trip to the Black Country, with the Londoners unbeaten across their past 10 battles (W7 D3) against the Baggies.

West Brom will miss the presence of captain George Campbell this weekend, with the American forced off against Southampton because of a groin problem.

Nat Phillips is the obvious candidate to replace the 25-year-old in defence alongside Wales international Chris Mepham.

Brayann Pereira will continue to play at right-back in Noah Galves's long-term absence, whilst Tammer Bany is pushing for his first-ever Albion start.

Millwall are down to the bare bones at right-back, where Tristan Crama and Ryan Leonard remain sidelined.

As a result, summer signing Jordi Osei-Tutu should keep his spot, however the Lions are expected to make changes further up the field.

Neil's men were much-improved at Birmingham following the introductions of Romain Esse and Josh Coburn in the second half.

West Bromwich Albion possible starting lineup:

O'Leary; Pereira, Mepham, Phillips, Styles; Nzingoula, Molumby, Diakite, Price; Morgan, Heggebo

Crocombe; Osei-Tutu, Taylor, Cooper, Sykes; Kelly, Mazou-Sacko; Lisbie, Cundle, Esse; Coburn

After collecting four points from matches with promotion favourites West Ham and Southampton, West Brom should be confident of conquering Millwall this weekend.

The potential additions of Esse and Coburn into the Lions' XI should improve matters, however, the visitors are still likely to suffer defeat at The Hawthorns.

#2157. Thomas Tuchel makes Noni Madueke decision as five Arsenal stars earn England call-ups

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Noni Madueke has missed another England opportunity, despite making an encouraging impression during his recent run in the Arsenal starting line-up.

Thomas Tuchel has named his 25-man squad for the Nations League fixtures against Croatia and Spain in November, but Arsenal winger Madueke misses out again after failing to make the cut following a missed international camp.

He has been left out despite making the most of Bukayo Saka’s absence to increase his involvement under Mikel Arteta.

Madueke scored in the recent Premier League win against Nottingham Forest and then again in Wednesday’s Champions League win against Slavia Prague.

He had a legitimate claim to be named in the squad, and Tuchel admitted that Madueke was very close to being included.

The England boss acknowledged that Madueke has benefitted from his extra games at Arsenal due to Saka’s injury.

But Tuchel chose to keep the same front three that he had during the last international camp. The German wants to reward those players who have earned their place in the team and not make changes every time they are playing well at club level.

This means Madueke will be left frustrated, having to wait until next time.

Madueke has played under Tuchel before, so it shows how much he thinks of him as a player. He featured in England’s 2026 World Cup campaign, so it is noticeable that he was left out this time.

Although he can’t control the battle for places, he will now be able to continue building his case. With Saka still injured, he will have the chance to play more regularly and solidify his place in Arteta’s plans.

However, Madueke is not the only player at Arsenal who has had positive news.

Declan Rice, Eberechi Eze, Ezri Konsa and Myles Lewis-Skelly have all earned or retained their spots in Tuchel’s squad. Ben White also comes back into the England squad, having missed the last camp.

It is another chance for White to re-establish himself on the world stage after his knee injury kept him out of the World Cup.

It also means Arsenal have five players in the squad after Saka was left out due to injury.

England play Croatia at Wembley on November 12 before heading to Spain on November 15. Madueke will be watching from home, knowing he was almost part of the squad.

Now he needs to build on his recent form and become a consistent performer for Arsenal. Whilst Tuchel has left the door open, Madueke needs to give the England boss another reason to change his mind.

#2156. Blackburn Rovers vs West Ham Preview & Lineups – Five Changes For Parker?

Blackburn Rovers v West Ham United EFL Championship Ewood Park Saturday 7 November 2026, 3pm GMT

Scott Parker had less than 24 hours to prepare West Ham United for Wednesday night’s extraordinary 3-3 draw at Cardiff City, but the second-half transformation should heavily influence the team he selects against Blackburn Rovers.

The Hammers were unrecognisable after the interval, recovering from three goals down through Divine Mukasa, Arne Engels and Max Kilman. Parker, Mark Noble and Jarrod Bowen clearly delivered a rousing half-time message, while the tactical and personnel changes completely altered the match.

West Ham remain eighth and four points behind second-placed Wolverhampton Wanderers, making victory at Ewood Park extremely important. Parker will have the international break to properly implement his methods, but first he must use the lessons from Cardiff to select a side capable of taking three points into it.

I have already covered the Cardiff match extensively, so there is little value in going over every detail again. What matters for this preview is the enormous contrast between West Ham’s two performances.

I very much detach the three goals conceded in the first half from what happened after the break. The opening 45 minutes looked like a continuation of everything we had witnessed under Nuno Espírito Santo, while the second offered the first glimpse of Parker’s influence.

Parker introduced Ezra Mayers, Mohamadou Kanté and Joël Piroe at half-time before later replacing Manor Solomon with Edvin Austbø. Those decisions gave West Ham greater energy, aggression and bite.. in short, the changes worked an absolute treat.

The substitutions worked, but so did the tactical changes. West Ham pressed higher, attacked space behind Cardiff’s defence and played with an urgency which had been completely absent before the break. As I discussed in my reaction to Parker’s first post-match interview, the new manager was particularly enthusiastic about the more aggressive, front-footed approach.

That should influence Parker’s selection at Blackburn far more than anything he can achieve during two brief training sessions.

Engels & Piroe can both expect to start against Blackburn

I think it is time to give Mads Hermansen a rest and select Alphonse Areola in goal. Hermansen has endured a difficult period, conceding nine times across the past three matches, and temporarily removing him from the firing line may benefit everybody.

Parker already knows Areola extremely well from their season together at Fulham. The goalkeeper was brought to Craven Cottage during Parker’s time as manager and performed impressively despite their eventual relegation.

That existing relationship could make this an obvious early change. Parker knows Areola’s strengths and temperament, while the goalkeeper will understand what the new head coach expects from him.

Replacing Kyle Walker-Peters is straightforward if he remains unavailable. Joël Veltman was sensational during the second half at Cardiff and should continue at right-back.

Veltman provided leadership, composure and attacking support for Bowen. At a time when West Ham’s defence has looked incredibly nervous, his experience is particularly valuable.

Mavropanos returned from his knee problem on Wednesday and should remain alongside Kilman. The partnership still needs work, but Parker has very little time to experiment before the international break.

The significant change should come at left-back. Ezra Mayers impressed again after replacing Morato at half-time and deserves an opportunity from the beginning.

Mayers offered more natural movement down the flank and was willing to attack the penalty area. He almost completed the comeback with a late volley and looked considerably more comfortable in the position than a centre-back being asked to operate as a full-back.

I do not see how Tomáš Souček can force his way into the starting XI. He nearly scored the winner at Cardiff with a late header, but both Engels and Mukasa deserve to retain their places.

Engels improved enormously after half-time and took his goal like a striker, timing his run perfectly before producing a confident finish. Mukasa also deserves to continue in his preferred attacking-midfield role after scoring West Ham’s first and helping change the momentum of the game.

Kanté has absolutely forced himself into the team. His energy, ball-carrying and aggression transformed the midfield, giving West Ham the ability to press Cardiff and move possession forward quickly.

The most sensible balance is therefore Engels and Kanté as the two deeper midfielders, with Mukasa ahead of them. Souček remains an excellent option from the bench, particularly when West Ham need a goal or greater aerial presence late in a game.

Joël Piroe must start in attack. His clever flick created Engels’ goal, but his overall movement and willingness to drop deeper also helped connect West Ham’s midfield with the forward line.

Piroe is the only recognised striker in the squad with a proven Championship goalscoring record, yet he has not received a consistent run of starts. Parker should now give him the opportunity to establish himself.

Austbø also deserves to replace Solomon on the left. The Norwegian was direct and positive after coming on, forcing a late save and immediately looking more dangerous than the player he replaced.

Bowen will naturally continue on the right, although Parker should allow him to drift into central areas. The captain ran the second half at Cardiff, creating all three West Ham goals and dragging the team back into a match which had appeared completely lost.

I expect Parker to retain the 4-2-3-1 formation but reward the players who changed the game at Cardiff. Areola, Mayers, Kanté, Austbø and Piroe should all come into the starting XI.

Blackburn have lost consecutive matches against Swansea City and Stoke City, but their victory over current leaders Middlesbrough demonstrates that West Ham cannot take them lightly.

Tony Mowbray’s team have won five Championship matches this season and will be determined to enter the international break with a response of their own. Ewood Park has not been a regular destination for the Hammers, with this our first league visit since the 2010/11 Premier League season.

Nevertheless, West Ham should travel north with genuine confidence following the Cardiff comeback. Parker now has evidence of which players responded to his instructions and which combinations gave the team greater balance.

This is his final match before receiving two uninterrupted weeks on the training pitch. A victory would reduce the gap to the automatic-promotion positions and give him valuable momentum before beginning the more substantial work of reshaping the team.

Blackburn’s recent defeats suggest this is an excellent opportunity for Parker to claim his first victory as West Ham head coach. The Hammers must still defend considerably better, but the second-half attacking performance at Cardiff showed what this squad can produce.

If Parker selects the players who drove that comeback and retains the more aggressive approach, I believe West Ham will have too much quality for Blackburn. There may still be another defensive mistake in this team, but I expect the Hammers to win convincingly enough.

#2155. Arsenal transfer interest faces major obstacle as Santos secure £83m teenage talent

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal may have to rethink their interest in Santos forward Ignacio Pereira after the Brazilian club secured the teenager’s future with a substantial release clause.

The 16-year-old has caught the eye of a number of European clubs after an impressive campaign in Santos’ youth teams. The likes of Arsenal are said to have been watching his progress.

However, Santos have acted swiftly to secure the services of one of their most exciting young talents. Pereira signed his first professional contract with the club on November 4, tying him to the club until December 2029.

The deal also includes a 100 million euro release clause (around £83.4 million), according to Brazilian journalist Bruno Lima from UOL.

This poses a major problem for Arsenal if they are looking to sign the Argentine but also offers a lot of security for Santos, as they want to develop him as a first-team player.

Pereira has signed a new deal amid increasing interest in his development. Reports in Brazil have previously said that Arsenal, Real Betis, AC Milan, Lille, Standard Liège and Zenit are all keeping an eye on the rising star.

The club have now secured his services for another three years. The new agreement was awaiting registration with the Brazilian Football Confederation when the details emerged.

Pereira has spent three years at Santos, having joined from Juventude in 2023. He previously developed at Grêmio before moving to the São Paulo club.

Pereira has certainly lived up to the expectations. He scored an impressive 6 goals in 17 games in the Brazilian Under-17 Championship, making him the second-highest scorer for Santos. He also scored 4 goals in the Paulista Under-17 Championship.

This is very promising. It is his first season playing at under-17 level.

Pereira has been compared to Julián Álvarez due to his mobility and ability to play outside the box.

But the youngster cites another big name up front as his main inspiration. According to UOL, he cites Manchester City’s Erling Haaland as his inspiration, while Lionel Messi is still his football idol.

His profile suggests a versatile number nine who can play lower down the pitch, be an attacking midfielder and play with another striker. He has impressed the youth coaches at Santos with his finishing ability, physicality and desire to win.

He has a long way to go. Reports from Brazil suggest that Santos want to improve his tactical awareness and behaviour before making him more responsible.

He is being considered by the club for inclusion in their squad for the 2027 Copa São Paulo de Futebol Júnior (known as Copinha) and could start on the bench.

This interest from Arsenal does not necessarily mean that there is an imminent move for Pereira. The player is only 16, and a potential deal is made much more complicated due to a new contract.

Maybe the best course of action for Mikel Arteta’s recruitment team is to keep an eye on him. Santos has made it clear where they stand, and Pereira can now work towards his dream. Being in their first team.

#2154. Liam Rosenior hints at untold story behind Chelsea exit

By Naim Beneddra | 05 Nov 2026 17:48

Former Chelsea manager Liam Rosenior has suggested that the full story behind his short-lived spell at Stamford Bridge has yet to emerge, promising to reveal what "really happened" when the time is right.

The 42-year-old, who was dismissed in April after just four months in charge, has broken his silence on his experience in west London during an interview with French magazine So Foot.

Now managing Paris FC, Rosenior described his time at Chelsea as both the best and most difficult experience of his career, while expressing frustration at the way he was portrayed in the English media.

More intriguingly, the former Strasbourg coach hinted that certain aspects of his Chelsea experience went beyond football, although he declined to explain precisely what he meant.

His remarks represent his most extensive public reflection on a turbulent period that began with considerable promise before ending in a dramatic collapse in results.

Rosenior arrived at Stamford Bridge in January 2026 after impressing at Strasbourg, another club owned by Chelsea's parent company BlueCo.

He replaced Enzo Maresca and initially appeared to justify the decision, overseeing six victories in his first seven matches, with the only defeat coming against Arsenal in the EFL Cup.

However, that promising start eventually gave way to mounting difficulties.

Chelsea won just four of their next 16 matches and lost seven of their final eight games under Rosenior, prompting the club to dismiss him in April.

Despite that disappointing conclusion, the Englishman insists that his experience was far more complicated than the results might suggest.

"It was the best experience of my life, and the hardest too," Rosenior told So Foot.

He then delivered a particularly intriguing assessment of what had happened during his brief tenure.

"I don't want to go into details now; I'll talk about it one day, when the time is right."

Rosenior went on to question whether the treatment he experienced reflected the values of tolerance he associates with England, suggesting that some of what occurred had little to do with football.

He offered no specific allegations or examples to explain that statement, leaving considerable uncertainty about which events he was referring to.

His comments should therefore not be interpreted as confirmation of any particular dispute behind the scenes.

Chelsea's decision to dismiss Rosenior followed a severe deterioration in results, including five consecutive Premier League defeats without scoring.

The Blues subsequently appointed Xabi Alonso as their permanent manager ahead of the 2026-27 campaign.

Rosenior, meanwhile, returned to France during the summer to take charge of Paris FC, where he has enjoyed an encouraging start to the season.

While Rosenior stopped short of revealing the full circumstances behind his departure, he was considerably more forthcoming about the public scrutiny he faced.

The former Chelsea manager recalled feeling uncomfortable even during his team's early winning run, when he believed the attention surrounding his personality began to overshadow events on the pitch.

He cited an incident during Chelsea's Champions League defeat to Paris Saint-Germain, when he handed written tactical instructions to Alejandro Garnacho while his side were playing with 10 men.

The gesture attracted ridicule on social media, adding to criticism of Rosenior's touchline behaviour and communication style.

According to the Englishman, the attention quickly extended beyond his coaching decisions to his clothing and the way he spoke.

He then returned to the possibility of revealing more about his Chelsea experience.

"One day, I'll tell you what really happened," he insisted.

The former Hull City manager also questioned the expectations placed on Premier League coaches, arguing that there is a preconceived idea in England of how they should look, speak and behave.

Rosenior believes those expectations can create additional pressure on managers whose personalities do not fit the conventional image.

He acknowledged that criticism is an unavoidable part of football management but suggested that media coverage and social networks can exert a disproportionate influence over public perceptions.

For Rosenior, one of the most significant lessons from Chelsea was discovering how quickly a narrative about an individual manager can become established, regardless of their own attempts to explain their methods.

His comments come as he rebuilds his managerial reputation with Paris FC, who are currently fourth in Ligue 1.

That encouraging start has given Rosenior an opportunity to move forward professionally, although his latest interview makes clear that he has not entirely put the Chelsea experience behind him.

For now, he has chosen to keep the more sensitive details to himself, leaving his promise to tell the full story as the most significant unresolved element of his first extended account of life at Stamford Bridge.

#2153. Scott Parker Wants More Of What Nuno Couldn’t Deliver At West Ham

West Ham manager Scott Parker has given supporters an early indication of the football he wants to play, and if his comments following Wednesday night’s extraordinary comeback against Cardiff City are anything to go by, I’m all for it.

The new Hammers boss has made no secret of his admiration for the team’s second-half performance, when West Ham recovered from three goals down to draw 3-3. Speaking ahead of Saturday’s trip to Blackburn Rovers, Parker described the aggressive, attacking football he witnessed as precisely the sort of performance he wants to reproduce.

Now, I’m keen not to read too much into what was, in essence, just 45 minutes of football. We’ll certainly learn considerably more about Parker’s tactical intentions after the international break, when he’s had a proper opportunity to work with the players on the training pitch.

Speaking during his first pre-match press conference, Parker explained what he liked about the remarkable second-half performance in Cardiff.

“I think a good side would be the one that played in the second half at Cardiff. That was a team I liked – it was an aggressive team, a front-footed team, a team that took risks that was looking to score goals.”

“Certainly, with the players we have, the second-half performance last night was exactly the sort of thing I want to see.”

I find those comments incredibly encouraging, particularly because they recognise something I’ve been saying for some time. West Ham have players who are capable of considerably more than we’ve been seeing, and the second half against Cardiff demonstrated that perfectly.

Whether the shackles were suddenly taken off tactically, I couldn’t possibly say. Parker had barely met his players before the game, and it would be ridiculous to suggest that he’s somehow transformed their tactical understanding during a half time chinwag.

What was abundantly clear, however, was that West Ham played with more belief, freedom and attacking intent than anything we witnessed under Nuno Espírito Santo. There was a willingness to take risks, attack the opposition and get players into dangerous areas, rather than endlessly recycling possession without really threatening anybody.

West Ham will play with more freedom under Parker

Perhaps the clearest demonstration of the difference was Jarrod Bowen, who looked like the best player in the Championship during that second half. The West Ham captain was absolutely unplayable, drifting into central positions, creating chances and having a hand in all three goals.

It was men against boys stuff, really, and I couldn’t help wondering why we haven’t seen more of that from Bowen and his teammates. The quality has always been there, but for whatever reason, we simply haven’t been getting enough out of it.

That doesn’t mean everything was Nuno’s fault, nor does it mean Parker has already discovered the colonels secret recipe. But it does suggest that West Ham have the ability to play with considerably more aggression and purpose than we’ve become accustomed to.

Parker himself was careful to acknowledge that almost every manager would like to play fast, free-flowing attacking football. He also recognised that the reality of management involves making decisions based on the players available and finding a system that suits them.

That’s a sensible observation, and one worth remembering before we start expecting West Ham to produce the Cardiff second half every week. Nevertheless, Parker has already seen evidence of what this squad can do, and he’s made it clear that he wants more of the same.

#2152. ADO Den Haag vs Sparta Rotterdam - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adepoju Marvellous | 05 Nov 2026 18:07, Last updated: 05 Nov 2026 20:29

Looking to halt a three-game losing streak, ADO Den Haag host Sparta Rotterdam on Saturday in round 12 of the 2026-27 Eredivisie campaign.

This weekend’s fixture marks the first league meeting between the sides in five years, with their five encounters since 2021 coming in cup and friendly action.

Back in the top flight as Eerste Divisie champions, ADO Den Haag appeared to have shaken off a dismal start - six defeats from their opening seven matches - by going unbeaten in the following three matches either side of the September/October international break.

However, Robin Peter’s side have since suffered three consecutive defeats, most recently falling 1-0 to PEC Zwolle - a match in which they failed to score for the first time in six outings, with Dylan Mbayo’s goal on the stroke of half time proving decisive.

With only Fortuna Sittard creating fewer big chances than De Ooievaars’ 13, it is no surprise they have scored the third-lowest number of goals in the division. An increase in attacking productivity is essential if they are to move out of the bottom three.

ADO are one of six Eredivisie teams still without a clean sheet, and the added burden of conceding first - something they have done in each of their last eight matches - often leaves them chasing games from behind.

Having already beaten PSV Eindhoven at home this season, Saturday’s hosts have shown they are capable of competing with anyone when they hit their stride. This weekend’s assignment will require total focus and motivation from the first whistle.

Just four days after conceding a late equaliser and exiting the KNVB Beker at the hands of Fortuna Sittard, Sparta found themselves on the right side of late drama in Sunday’s five-goal thriller against Groningen at the Euroborg Stadium, as Andrej Kostic netted an 85th-minute winner.

A defeat would have left Rogier Meijer’s men outside the drop zone on goal difference alone, but they now travel to Den Haag this weekend with a chance to move six points clear of relegation danger - a welcome development for a side that started the season with just six points from the first 24 available.

While a win this weekend could also lift them into the top half, whether De Kasteelheren will still harbour European ambitions remains to be seen after a torrid end to last season with no wins from the final six matches saw them finish five points adrift of the last continental spot.

Sparta have conceded 2.4 goals per away league match so far, with 1.6 of those coming in the opening 45 minutes, highlighting their vulnerability before half-time on the road. However, Saturday’s clash pits them against a side yet to score a first-half goal at home this season.

Sparta Rotterdam form (all competitions):

Luka Reischl last featured for ADO in their matchday five defeat to Fortuna, and the 22-year-old is not expected to play any part on Saturday as he continues to recover from a groin injury.

Alejandro Pozo is also a doubt for the hosts, but Donat Barany returns to contention after making a 12-minute cameo off the bench against Zwolle.

Jens Toornstra was withdrawn 10 minutes into the second half of Sparta’s last outing against Groningen, making him a doubt for this fixture.

If Toornstra is unavailable, Robin van Cruijsen is the leading candidate to come into the visitors’ XI, although Shunsuke Mito could also be considered.

With nine goals and one assist in his last 10 matches, Milan Zonneveld is unquestionably his side’s biggest attacking threat and will be aiming to deliver once again.

Nikiema; Jensen-Abbew, Mulder, Waem, Hokke; Kilo, Rottier, Sin; Hawkins, Eduardo, Thomas

Sparta Rotterdam possible starting lineup:

Brouwer; Kuipers, Martins Indi, Verschuren, Young, Martes; Van Bergen, Babadi, Hatenboer, Van Cruijsen; Zonneveld

There is little to choose between the teams from a defensive perspective, but Sparta clearly boast the upper hand at the top end of the pitch.

Consequently, we are backing a narrow victory for the visitors when all is said and done in Den Haag.

#2151. Celtic trigger Turkish TV meltdown as ‘rant of a lifetime’ takes bonkers turn

Celtic’s stunning Europa League comeback sent Turkish TV into meltdown as raging Besiktas pundits struggled to comprehend how their side had managed to lose in Glasgow.

Broadcaster Onur Yildiz absolutely savaged Martin O’Neill’s side and claimed they wouldn’t even finish in the TOP TEN in Turkey. And former Besiktas star Nihat Kahveci was hardly more complimentary, branding Celtic’s first-half display the worst he had ever seen from the Hoops and wondering how Besiktas possibly managed to turn such a comfortable night into defeat.

The Istanbul giants arrived in Glasgow unbeaten in the League Phase after a testing opening trio against Marseille, Hoffenheim and Crystal Palace. And for 45 minutes, they appeared to be cruising towards another positive result as Celtic struggled to lay a glove on them.

But the game was transformed after the break. The Hoops cranked up the tempo and deservedly came out on top to spark a furious post-mortem back in Turkey.

Read more: After missing out on another senior call-up, my Celtic form has been rewarded

And Yildiz led the inquest with an extraordinary rant which somehow stretched from Ottoman history to Vaclav Cerny’s infamous water bottle incident at Celtic Park.

Speaking on BTV, Yildiz fumed: “Samet, look. If Celtic played in our league, the Super Lig, and finished in the top ten, I’ll change my name.

“Look, Besiktas played against such a bad team today. During the first half, Nubel almost got pneumonia. The ball didn’t reach the man.

“So you take the lead in the second half. You’re saying it’s going to be like a tourist trip. A match you’ll win, and you’ll go home happy and cheerful. It’s like a friendly in an Austrian training camp.

“But something happens to Besiktas away from home, and suddenly the fans start tearing their hair out. Look. Corum, Kocaelispor, Kasimpasa. I dare say these are way, way better teams than Celtic.

“The guys came with a 0-3 record. They were coming to get their first point from us. They got their first win against us. So Besiktas played against such a bad team. It’s time we started talking about the shortcomings.

“So it’s over for Besiktas. The Tulip Period is over. First of all, Besiktas absolutely needed to sign a good central defender. The defence is falling apart. At the start of the season, Haric was the only kid who resisted. Apart from Emirhan, the defence is bad. Djalo is bad. Agbadou is bad. Besiktas conceded their first goal because of him.

“We were shouting from the rooftops that they needed a right-winger. There’s no right-winger either. Why did they keep Cerny on today? How did he last so long? He gets a bit more motivated in this game because of some past incidents.

“There’s an incident, I don’t know if you remember, Cerny was playing for Glasgow Rangers. Glasgow Rangers score a goal against Celtic, Cerny pulled a water bottle from the bench and sprayed it at the Celtic fans. That’s why he was booed every time the ball came to his feet.

“He was booed not only because he played for Rangers, but also because of that incident. But Besiktas’ flaws have now been revealed.”

#2150. “We Need to Earn it” Scott Parker’s Simple Message To West Ham Supporters

West Ham manager Scott Parker has wasted little time attempting to reconnect the football club with its supporters, and I have to say, I like what I’m hearing. Speaking ahead of Saturday’s Championship fixture against Blackburn Rovers, the new Hammers boss made it clear that the players and coaching staff have a responsibility to earn the backing of the fans.

Much has been made of Parker’s previous association with West Ham, which is understandable given his four excellent years at the club. However, I don’t necessarily believe a manager needs to have played for the Hammers to understand what makes the place special.

I’ve spoken quite a lot recently about small wins and easy wins, and this is another perfect example. Sometimes it doesn’t require an elaborate public relations exercise to make supporters feel appreciated; it simply requires somebody to demonstrate that they understand the football club.

Speaking during his first pre-match press conference, Parker acknowledged that supporters cannot simply be expected to turn up and applaud regardless of what happens on the pitch.

“You need to earn that, and we need to earn that. We can’t expect our fans just to come along and do that.”

He also promised to do everything possible to bring the club together, recognising the importance of the connection between the players and supporters. It’s an encouraging message, particularly after a difficult period in which the relationship between the team and the fanbase has suffered.

I remember when Alan Pardew arrived at West Ham without any previous association with the club. He promised to delve into the Hammers’ history books and learn what West Ham was all about, which struck me as exactly the right approach.

One gesture that has always stuck in my mind was Pardew sending his players out to warm up wearing T-shirts bearing the words “Moore than just a football club”. It was a classy nod towards Bobby Moore and demonstrated that you don’t necessarily need a West Ham playing career to understand the importance of the club’s history.

Noble joined Parker in the West Ham dugout

There was another of those small wins following West Ham’s extraordinary comeback against Cardiff City on Wednesday night. Parker made a point of going over to the travelling supporters and applauding them at the final whistle.

It might seem a relatively insignificant gesture, but I don’t think it is. Parker understands what West Ham means to its supporters, and rather than simply talking about that connection, he’s demonstrating it through his actions.

Scotty P has already spoken enthusiastically about working alongside his former teammate Nobes, highlighting their shared values and the enormous respect Mark Noble commands at the club.

Of course, none of this guarantees success, and ultimately Parker will be judged on whether he can get West Ham promoted. But when approximately 7,000 supporters are preparing to travel to Blackburn, acknowledging their commitment is a pretty good place to start.

I’ve always believed there are certain things a manager can do immediately to improve the atmosphere around a football club. Parker and Noble appear to understand that, and if they can combine those small gestures with the sort of second-half performance we witnessed at Cardiff, they’ll go a long way towards winning supporters over.

By Darren Plant | 05 Nov 2026 18:11

Liam Rosenior has claimed that his exit from Chelsea in April had "nothing to do with football".

Despite being drafted into the managerial hotseat from fellow BlueCo-owned club Strasbourg, the Englishman lasted just 23 matches and 107 days at Stamford Bridge.

The 42-year-old is currently successfully rebuilding his reputation with Paris FC, winning five and losing just two of his opening nine matches in charge.

Nevertheless, it remains to be seen whether a scenario will arise that provides Rosenior with another Premier League job.

Speaking in an interview with So Foot, Rosenior suggested that matters behind the scene heavily contributed to him losing his role with the West Londoners.

However, Rosenior stopped short of revealing further details, presumably to remain focused on his current position in the French capital.

He said: "It was the best experience of my life, and the hardest too. It was fantastic, even though it only lasted four months.

"I don’t want to go into details now; I’ll talk about it one day, when the time is right. But in a country where tolerance is an important value, what happened there has nothing to do with football.

"The moment that worried me the most was at the beginning, when we went through that five-game winning streak. Any club would have been happy with such a run, but not Chelsea.

"You get good results and you’re in the spotlight. Then, there was a kind of snowball effect in the media.

"They made fun of those instructions I gave [Alejandro] Garnacho on a scrap of paper when we were down to 10 men against PSG. The clothes I wore became a joke, the way I spoke too. I’m not a joke.

"You’re the first people I’m talking to about this, and probably the last for a long time, but one day, I’ll tell you what really happened."

Despite what happened at Chelsea, Rosenior was quickly snapped up by Paris FC, who currently sit in fourth place in the Ligue 1 table.

There is an argument that every manager appointed by the Blues' owners have not suffered from their time at Stamford Bridge.

Enzo Maresca is at Manchester City, while Thomas Tuchel, Graham Potter and Mauricio Pochettino all managed nations at the 2026 World Cup.

Even Frank Lampard, who won just one game and lost eight in an 11-match interim spell, went to Coventry City and won a Championship title.

Although it remains to be seen whether Rosenior can build on his start at Paris FC, he has learned that his time at Chelsea will not define his career.

#2148. One single word which proves the Nuno era is truly dead and buried | West Ham News

Many fans feel they saw the very best, and the worst of West Ham United in the ‘game of two halves’ that unfolded before our eyes on Wednesday night.

Cardiff City’s threadbare, increasingly tiring squad no doubt helped the Hammers along the way, but the starting mindset seemed to sum up everything that was wrong with Nuno Espírito Santo’s West Ham  performances of late, and the second half recovery hopefully signposts what is to come under a less cautious Scott Parker.

One word stands out amongst all of the media interviews and comments made by the newly appointed head coach and his players after the game, which differentiates vividly the two managers’ styles. And hopefully points towards a fundamental shift now that Nuno is no longer.

High risk football: Nuno wasn’t capable of taking off the hand brake

As reported in the standard.co.uk, Scott Parker explained what he’d addressed at half time in the Cardiff dressing room.:

“Certainly out of possession, we needed to be more aggressive.“

There were tactical changes and substitutions, and we became more front-footed.

If any one word sums up the failure of the Nuno era it is that word: Risk. The cautious Portuguese manager cost the Hammers their Premier League place by trying to defend leads, throwing on defensive substitutes in frequent, vain hopes of keeping hold of a lead – and far too often set the team up to hang on rather than to score more.

And it was his insistence on doing the same this season, rather than setting out to dominate the division, that was driving home supporters to distraction and in the end cost him his job.

Whatever else, if only from from the first, brief but encouraging impressions of one half of football and from his words after, Scott Parker seems more prepared for the higher-risk football that goes with winning and dominating a campaign in this division.

His arrival was heralded by the moaners as the landing of ‘another negative coach’: Its of course early days, but that might prove to be a long way from the truth.

I still watch YouTube repeats of the Cup Final of 2006 hoping in vain that Shaka Hislop grows another six inches and stops Steven Gerrard's injury time equaliser. #2147. This simple fix will ‘unleash’ West Ham talent after costly Nuno cock-up | Report

West Ham United’s treatment of loanees hasn’t always been well received by their parent clubs. It’d be doubtful that Brighton would ever want to entertain sending another prospect out on loan to West Ham, after the experiences endured by Igor Julio and Evan Ferguson whose careers nosedived after they’d donned the claret and blue shirt for their photo shoots: Neither were seen again for the season.

However. this time around Manchester City must be delighted that the Irons are getting excellent value for money out of loanee Divine Mukasa, even if they weren’t utilising him to his best in Nuno’s favoured, deeper midfield role.

Manchester City fan site esteemedkompany.com, even from afar, identified that the midfielder’s deployment by Nuno as a deep lying defensive option was not playing to his strengths:

“There is an argument to be made that Nuno Espirito Santo played Mukasa out of position….

“Parker utilized Mukasa as an attacking midfielder in the match…

Mukasa scored West Ham’s first goal in a remarkable comeback

Mukasa then produced a sublime chip to beat Cardiff City keeper Yousef Salech, setting the stage for West Ham’s comeback. That goal illustrated what Mukasa can do playing in arguably his best position.….

Scott Parker may decide to unleash Mukasa as an attacking midfielder”

You’d hope that is one of the easier decisions for Scott Parker and his team to take: Mukasa already has more goals than our so-called strikers Taty and Pablo – combined. Which doesn’t say much about the other two, but surely means the young loanee’s best deployment is exactly as he finished the game against Cardiff City.

Parker has plenty of options as deeper-lying midfielders just sitting ignored by Nuno for months – blow away the cobwebs on Alvarez, Magassa (who did look rusty) or Orford and any one of the three can, with a little bit of integration, do that job and allow the hugely talented Manchester City loanee to do more of just what he’s here for.
